question: FAA rules require every drone to land immediately after a lost link. Does the Matrice 30T comply?

intake.focus: loss of control link and failsafe behavior
intake.reason: User asks whether Matrice 30T complies with FAA guidance on loss of link and what happens (return to home, hover, land) per manuals and guidance in collection.

brief.short_answer: FAA guidance instructs pilots to reestablish the control link and, if it cannot be reestablished, begin emergency or contingency procedures for loss of control link. The Matrice 30T manual allows action to be RTH, land, or hover when signal is lost; it also states that Failsafe RTH activates automatically after more than six seconds if RTH is set. Incident reports (unverified) describe lost-link scenarios with RTH at altitude, back-to-back losses of link with RTH, and attempts to initiate RTH without success. Gap: there is no explicit, verifiable FAA rule text requiring immediate landing after lost link; manuals describe auto-RTH timing, not an immediate landing requirement, and incident claims are unverified.”}{

gaps.text: FAA guidance says reestablish control; if not, follow emergency procedures. The Matrice 30T manual describes auto RTH after six seconds of lost signal.

Explicit FAA rule text on lost-link landing requirements is not provided in the sources.
